column2: The Oak of Ages

For months you have felt the heart of Athel Loren drawing you in. At last you answer the call and step into the Oak of Ages. The ancient wood closes around you and the mercy and wisdom of Isha flood your being. What happens in the dark of the tree cannot be put into words, but the one who walks out is far more than an elf. The Everqueen of the forest has woken.

For months you have felt the heart of Athel Loren drawing you in. At last you answer the call and step into the Oak of Ages. The ancient wood closes around you and the wrath and hunger of Kurnous burn through your being. What happens in the dark of the tree cannot be put into words, but the one who walks out wears antlers and is far more than an elf. The Lord of the Hunt has woken.
Let my light shine over the glades.
Let the Wild Hunt ride anew!
Winter draws near and once again the Oak of Ages calls you. You will rest within the heart of Athel Loren and wake with the first green of spring, and the forest will wait with you.
Winter draws near and once again the Oak of Ages calls you. As the year dies, so must you: you will burn, die and be reborn from the heart of Athel Loren when spring comes.
Summer is at an end and each day you feel heavier and slower. The sap runs thick. The call of Athel Loren bids you sink into torpor and sleep until spring.
So be it.
The year dies, and so do I.
Sleep...
Spring brings new life and colour to the woods. You wake from your long sleep, filled again with the power of Athel Loren and ready to defend it.
The forest wakes.

Something is wrong. You have woken with a terrible thirst for blood. The minds of every Great Hunter of Athel Loren shriek inside your skull, demanding that you guard the sacred glades and slaughter all who would do them harm. Every spirit and beast that hears your horn will be swept up in the frenzy.
Sound the horns! The Hunt rides!
This year Kurnous has woken mad with bloodlust. His horn already echoes over the glades, calling every creature of the forest to the hunt and driving spirits and beasts alike into a frenzy.
Blreaaarh!!!
The horns pierce my ears!
What is all that noise?
The Weave is out of balance. Day after day whispers and shrieks crawl beneath your bark, and it grows ever harder to think, to stay calm, to remember who you are.
Blreaaarh!!!
Athel Loren is not kind to those who do not respect its borders. Overnight the branches and roots twisted of their own will, and where part of your hold stood there is now only deep forest.
What... where did it go?

For weeks your spouse [asrai_spirit_victim.GetFirstName] was plagued by nightmares and visions of eyes among the leaves. Then one morning [asrai_spirit_victim.GetSheHe] was gone. You searched for days and lost four scouts to the treacherous forest before you gave up. The ancient spirits of Athel Loren have claimed [asrai_spirit_victim.GetHerHim] for your blasphemy, to wander the timeless glades forever.
Why!?

For three days your spouse [asrai_spirit_victim.GetFirstName] avoided you. When you finally force your way into [asrai_spirit_victim.GetHerHis] chamber you see why. The spirits, angered by your deeds, have carved their spite into [asrai_spirit_victim.GetHerHis] face.
This is... ugh!

Your [asrai_spirit_victim.GetSonDaughter] [asrai_spirit_victim.GetFirstName] walked into the woods and never came back. You searched for days and lost four scouts to the treacherous forest before you gave up. The ancient spirits of Athel Loren have claimed [asrai_spirit_victim.GetHerHim] for your blasphemy, to wander the timeless glades forever.

Your young [asrai_spirit_victim.GetSonDaughter] [asrai_spirit_victim.GetFirstName] has vanished from [asrai_spirit_victim.GetHerHis] bed. The cruel spirits of Athel Loren took what was dearest to you to punish your blasphemy, and the poor child will wander the timeless glades forever. Sometimes, at dusk, you think you hear [asrai_spirit_victim.GetHerHim] laughing among the trees.
No!
You wake in the night to something rasping under the sheets. You can neither see nor touch it, yet you feel cold claws working their way beneath your skin.
Help!
You wake in the night to something rasping under the sheets. You can neither see nor touch it, yet you feel cold claws working their way beneath your skin, searching for your eyes and your mouth.
Help!
You wake in the night to something rasping under the sheets. You can neither see nor touch it, yet you feel cold claws working their way beneath your skin, snapping bones and twisting limbs.
Grlllbllch...

Walking alone in the woods of Athel Loren is never wise. Yet here you are, with no idea how or why you left the safety of your hold. Voices whisper all around you and faint laughter echoes through the leaves. Every path leads deeper in.
Where am I? Help!

Your lover [asrai_spirit_victim.GetFirstName] spoke of nightmares and of voices in the leaves, and then one night [asrai_spirit_victim.GetSheHe] did not come to you. Your servants searched the forest edge and found only a ring of white flowers. The spirits of Athel Loren have taken [asrai_spirit_victim.GetHerHim] to punish you.
Why!?

[asrai_spirit_victim.GetTitledFirstName] has been missing for some days. [asrai_spirit_victim.GetSheHeCap] last spoke of a music in the trees that no one else could hear. Most of the court believes the spirits of Athel Loren have taken [asrai_spirit_victim.GetHerHim].
Perhaps the forest will give [asrai_spirit_victim.GetHerHim] back...
You cannot sleep and you cannot think. The shrieking voices of the angered spirits follow your every step, and day by day you feel your grip on your mind slipping.
Leave me alone! Alone!!
The spirits of Athel Loren are capricious and strange, all too ready to kill or twist any creature that trespasses in their woods. Only an offering may calm them, and even then only for a time.
A great offering for our friends.
The greatest gift for our friends.
I have changed my mind.
The mood of the forest is hard to read, but as your offering vanishes into the undergrowth you feel the Weave hum with approval.
Excellent.
The mood of the forest is hard to read. Within a day your offering is gone, but the spirits send no sign at all.
Hmm...

Your end has not come yet. Burning with righteous anger, your spirit flew back to the heart of Athel Loren and was reborn from the husk of a deadwood as twisted tree kin, ready to take vengeance on your enemies.
Raahhh!!
It grows harder and harder to recall your former life. The call of the forest is ever louder, and at last your mind slips away and merges with the Weave.
It grows harder and harder to recall your former life. The call of the forest is ever louder, but you feel you could still hold yourself apart from it, for a while.
It is time to join the Weave.
My time has not yet come!
You have stained your hands with the blood of the Avatar of Isha. Such a crime echoes across the Weave and drives every spirit of Athel Loren into a frenzy. No Asrai will follow you now.
You have stained your hands with the blood of the Avatar of Kurnous. Such a crime echoes across the Weave and drives every spirit of Athel Loren into a frenzy. No Asrai will follow you now.
You have stained your hands with the blood of [From.GetFirstName], a spirit of the forest. Such a crime echoes across the Weave and drives the other beings of Athel Loren into a frenzy.
What have I done!?
Bleaarrk'k'k'k!!!
[FromFrom.GetFirstName], one of the strange and treacherous Fair Folk, has carried off your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName] and means never to give [From.GetHerHim] back.
Cursed elves!
You have spent so long in the magical and secret lands of the elves that you can barely remember any other life. Mortal food tastes of ash and you hear music in the trees that others do not.
Where do I belong?
Your ward [From.GetFirstName] is coming of age, and the once delicate features of the child are being spoiled by the coarse traits of [From.GetHerHis] lesser race.
Send this thing back where it came from.
I am still fond of it.
Your glorious host has taken [From.GetName]. The people cower behind their doors and the hounds are hungry. What should be done?
Let nothing stand in our way!
Pick out the interesting ones.
Tread lightly in these foreign lands.
The merciless riders of [From.GetTitledFirstName] have brought ruin to your lands, burning every building they came across and hunting down your people like beasts.
Monsters!
The merciless riders of [From.GetTitledFirstName] have brought ruin to [FromFrom.GetName], burning every building they came across and hunting down the people like beasts.

The merciless riders of [From.GetTitledFirstName] have hunted down the people of [FromFrom.GetName] like beasts. Some they did not kill. They rounded them up and rode off with them into a magical mist, and no one knows what fate awaits them in the forest.
An ancient spirit has come out of the depths of the forest to honour your court with its presence, bringing its host to defend your glades.
We thank our new friend.

The great and ancient [From.GetFirstName] has taken an interest in [asrai_spirit_prey.GetTitledFirstName]. The spirit plainly wishes to draw [asrai_spirit_prey.GetHerHim] down into the depths of Athel Loren, forever.
Everything, for our friends from beyond.
No, not [asrai_spirit_prey.GetHerHim].
Your disrespect has so angered [From.GetFirstName], one of the ancient spirits of your glade, that [From.GetSheHe] has left your court in disgust, and [From.GetHerHis] host with [From.GetHerHim].
I am so sorry!
You called on the spirits, but they did not hear you. Nobody came.
They have abandoned us.
A host of saplings and dryads steps out of the trees and gathers under your banners, ready to fall on the enemies of the forest.
Let us hunt together!
The forest itself marches. A host of spirits led by ancient treemen appears from the trees and gathers under your banners, ready to fall on the enemies of the forest.
The Weave blesses us!
Summer has passed, and the spirits in your army are sinking into the torpor of winter. One by one they walk back into the forest.
No cell will hold you while the forces of Athel Loren are with you. Roots split the walls and the door falls open.
The forest has freed me.
Holding the Avatar of Isha inside Athel Loren was folly. The goddess walked free, and a legion of angry forest spirits went with her.
Holding the Avatar of Kurnous inside Athel Loren was folly. The god broke his bonds and a horde of angry spirits tore down your walls to free him.
Athel Loren is bound to its spirits. The one you tried to hold slipped away into the very ground of its home.
Damnation.
The Forest Fights Back
Spirits fall on the supply lines, and soldiers go mad or simply vanish into the wilds. Your troops are plainly not welcome in the glades of Athel Loren.
Keep together and keep your eyes open.

A silent group of elves in green and brown passed one of your camps last evening and told one of your captains that they will fight with you against a common enemy. By morning they were gone, leaving no tracks.
We welcome any help from our distant cousins.
Welcome, friends.
As if a little help will make us forget!
Who are these people?
The Weave has led an old spellsinger into your glade. The traveller remembers little of the road that brought them here, but they are ready to put themselves at your service.
It is a sign. They are welcome.
It might be cursed.

All the children of Isha are bound to the Weave, but you have always felt the forest more keenly than the others. The trees seem to whisper when you pass. Perhaps your guardian could teach you to listen, and to sing back.
I will be a wise spellsinger!
For some time now your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName] has been pestering you, begging you to teach [From.GetHerHim] how to touch the Weave and cast spells.
You may have some potential...
Go away. This is not a game.
Your guardian has agreed to take you as an apprentice and teach you the ways of the Weave.
I will soon be a powerful spellsinger!
Your [GetFromRelation] refused to teach you magic, claiming you lack what it takes to handle such a dangerous power.
I could! How can you say that?
There is much a spellsinger must know before the Weave can be trusted to them. What should [From.GetFirstName] learn next?
A spellsinger must tell light from darkness.
A spellsinger must always strive for perfection.
A spellsinger must never lose their calm.
Enough. Let us turn to the Weave itself.
For weeks you and your [GetFromRelation] have talked of how a spellsinger must keep a clear mind and judge the world without favour, lest they be deceived by the lies of Chaos or of lesser races.
Of course. We are the enlightened kin.
For weeks you and your [GetFromRelation] have talked of how a spellsinger must always work at their best: studying new songs, perfecting every ritual, leaving nothing to chance.
I would not want to blow anything up. By mistake.
For weeks you and your [GetFromRelation] have talked of how a spellsinger must stay calm, lest passion cloud the senses and twist the spell against its caster.
But is it not passion that gives purpose to the Hunt?

All in Athel Loren is balance: summer and winter, death and rebirth, light and darkness. The great cycles of the seasons rule the lives of all beings, and the Asrai do not shun any part of the Weave. Highweavers heal and preserve, while Darkweavers hunt, twist and terrify the forest's enemies. Which path calls to you?
I will follow the path of light.
I will follow the dark path.
It has become clear that your student [From.GetFirstName] has chosen the path of the Highweaver, to heal the sickness and corruption that would tarnish the forest and keep it pure.
It has become clear that your student [From.GetFirstName] has chosen the path of the Darkweaver, to twist and terrify those who would harm Athel Loren.
I am proud of [From.GetHerHim].
That is... still acceptable, I suppose.
You have taught your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName] much of what you know over the years. Is [From.GetSheHe] ready to be named a spellsinger?
The time has come.
No. [From.GetSheHeCap] never will be.
After many years of study, your [GetFromRelation] has named you a spellsinger, an apprentice no longer. The Weave answers when you sing to it now.
And yet there is so much still to learn...
Your [GetFromRelation] has judged you unfit to be a spellsinger and sent you away. Your years of study are over.
Years wasted!

Spellsingers are the mages of the Asrai. Through their bond with the Weave of Athel Loren they can reshape the forest around them. After your long studies, your liege has given you a place at court among them.
The forest speaks to me.
You have spent decades poring over ancient lore, meditating deep in the forest and seeking visions from the spirits, all for nothing. Your gift for magic is mediocre at best.
There is no point going on...
You have dwelt in darkness so long that its taint has begun to cloud your senses, filling you with senseless hatred and foul thoughts. The balance must be restored.
Light to balance the darkness.
I shall endure it.

Your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName] is plagued by [From.GetHerHis] dealings with the dark powers. As a Highweaver it is your duty to restore the balance of [From.GetHerHis] soul so that [From.GetSheHe] can go on serving the forest.
I will prepare the ritual.
The ritual of [From.GetTitledFirstName] has calmed your troubled soul. The dark powers are bound to your will once more, to be unleashed only on the enemies of Athel Loren.
And soon they will be.
For all [From.GetTitledFirstName]'s efforts, you are still plagued by bloody visions and twisted dreams. The dark powers you have called on to flay your enemies are devouring your soul.
I *will* contain them!
